results.name: participant_yes_rate_sd
results.description: SD across participants (participant = run of rows starting at trial_index 0) of the overall yes rate; observed > model means the model (no individual differences) under-produces between-person variation in response bias.
results.code:
# name: participant_yes_rate_sd
# description: SD across participants (participant = run of rows starting at trial_index 0) of the overall yes rate; observed > model means the model (no individual differences) under-produces between-person variation in response bias.
def test_statistic(df):
    pid = (df["trial_index"].to_numpy() == 0).cumsum()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    m = pd.Series(r).groupby(pid).mean()
    return float(m.std(ddof=0)) if len(m) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: far_unrelated_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for "unrelated" targets: >=25 away from every example, sharing no last digit with any example, and of opposite parity when all examples share a parity; observed > model means the model under-produces baseline/lapse yeses far from the examples.
results.code:
# name: far_unrelated_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for "unrelated" targets: >=25 away from every example, sharing no last digit with any example, and of opposite parity when all examples share a parity; observed > model means the model under-produces baseline/lapse yeses far from the examples.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - tg[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    same_last = (valid & (np.mod(ex, 10) == np.mod(tg, 10)[:, None])).any(axis=1)
    par = np.mod(ex, 2)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    n_odd = np.where(valid, par, 0).sum(axis=1)
    all_even = n_odd == 0
    all_odd = n_odd == n
    tpar = np.mod(tg, 2)
    parity_ok = ~((all_even & (tpar == 0)) | (all_odd & (tpar == 1)))
    sel = (d >= 25) & (~same_last) & parity_ok
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    return float(r[sel].mean()) if sel.any() else 0.0

results.name: proximity_gradient
results.description: Among targets not in the set, yes rate when the nearest example is 1-5 away minus yes rate when it is 16-30 away; observed > model means the model's numerical-similarity generalization is too flat (people generalize more sharply to nearby numbers), observed < model the reverse.
results.code:
# name: proximity_gradient
# description: Among targets not in the set, yes rate when the nearest example is 1-5 away minus yes rate when it is 16-30 away; observed > model means the model's numerical-similarity generalization is too flat (people generalize more sharply to nearby numbers), observed < model the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    d = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - tg[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    near = (d >= 1) & (d <= 5)
    far = (d >= 16) & (d <= 30)
    if not near.any() or not far.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near].mean() - r[far].mean())

results.name: target_in_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets that equal one of the shown examples; observed < model means the model over-endorses the examples themselves (people do not always say yes to a shown number), observed > model the reverse.
results.code:
# name: target_in_set_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets that equal one of the shown examples; observed < model means the model over-endorses the examples themselves (people do not always say yes to a shown number), observed > model the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    inset = (ex == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    return float(r[inset].mean()) if inset.any() else 0.0

results.name: parity_match_effect
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples that all share a parity, yes rate for non-example targets of that parity minus those of the opposite parity; observed > model means the model under-weights parity (odd/even) generalization, observed < model means it over-weights it.
results.code:
# name: parity_match_effect
# description: In sets of >=2 examples that all share a parity, yes rate for non-example targets of that parity minus those of the opposite parity; observed > model means the model under-weights parity (odd/even) generalization, observed < model means it over-weights it.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    n_odd = np.where(valid, np.mod(ex, 2), 0).sum(axis=1)
    same = (n >= 2) & ((n_odd == 0) | (n_odd == n))
    set_par = (n_odd > 0).astype(float)
    inset = (ex == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    match = np.mod(tg, 2) == set_par
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    a = same & ~inset & match
    b = same & ~inset & ~match
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index >= 225 minus yes rate on earlier trials; a nonzero observed value beyond the model's means the model (no time dependence) misses a drift in willingness to say yes over the session.

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 5 of the first example (and >10 from the last) minus yes rate for targets within 5 of the last example (and >10 from the first); observed < model means the model over-produces primacy (first-example-anchored guessing) relative to people.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
# description: In sets of >=3 examples, yes rate for non-example targets within 5 of the first example (and >10 from the last) minus yes rate for targets within 5 of the last example (and >10 from the first); observed < model means the model over-produces primacy (first-example-anchored guessing) relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tg = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    first = ex[:, 0]
    idx = np.clip(n - 1, 0, ex.shape[1] - 1)
    last = ex[np.arange(len(ex)), idx]
    inset = (np.where(valid, ex, -1) == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    df1 = np.abs(tg - first)
    dl = np.abs(tg - last)
    base = (n >= 3) & ~inset
    a = base & (df1 <= 5) & (dl > 10)
    b = base & (dl <= 5) & (df1 > 10)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
